primary_access.access: abstract-only
primary_access.scope: The authentic human FTD mutation source is retained; complete original experiments were not recovered. Independent full 20223751 patient-fibroblast/cell data corroborate endolysosomal abnormalities, but do not reconstruct every original compartment assay.

primary_access.access: selected full
primary_access.scope: Actual yeast Vta1/Vps4 Results, Figure1 and recycling Methods were read. The paper establishes Vta1-dependent regulation of Vps4 and ESCRT recycling, not direct human CHMP2B ATPase or membrane-fusion chemistry. Conserved MVB context is retained separately from the unresolved exact fusion-step assertions.

primary_access.access: selected partial despite full flag
primary_access.scope: Selected text contains abstract/Introduction/Discussion but lacks complete Results/Methods; bounded original PMC routes did not recover the target-specific CHMP2B assay. Do not infer wrong-paralog curation from the hVps24/CHMP3 title. Independent target evidence supports the retained broad MVB role.

primary_access.access: abstract plus literal target record
primary_access.scope: The exact CHMP2B–CHMP3 positive two-hybrid physical-association record is reproduced. The selected cache is abstract-only; the complete primary construct protocol was not recovered. Binding is retained at the measured assay scope.

primary_access.access: abstract-only
primary_access.scope: Authentic human ALS mutation/phenotype abstract. It supports contextual neuronal-maintenance biology, without complete genotype/assay reconstruction or uniform loss-of-function claims.

primary_access.access: abstract-only plus independent corroboration
primary_access.scope: The abstract explicitly identifies mouse mSnf7-2 binding to WT CHMP2B and stronger association with CHMP2BIntron5, plus mutant autophagic/neurodegenerative effects. Full Methods were not recovered. Human CHMP4B association in 21975012 is independent corroboration, not a replacement of the original mouse partner.

primary_access.access: selected abstract; authentic indexed full external
primary_access.scope: Actual indexed author-uploaded Results/structure/Methods establish the CHMP2B195–213 C-terminal MIM and VPS4 MIT binding, including PDB2JQK. No selected main cache was overwritten. VPS4 supplies ATP hydrolysis; binding does not make CHMP2B an ATPase.

primary_access.access: selected full and independently retrieved correct XML
primary_access.scope: Full main Results/Methods/legends and supplemental-description text were read. Mutant human CHMP2B clearance effects are positive; p62 immuno-EM is not a direct CHMP2B compartment localization assay. Precise target membrane assertions remain unresolved. The erroneous unrelated PMC2064791 retrieval was explicitly excluded; correct article PMC2064794 XML was identity-checked.

primary_access.access: selected partial; exact author-hosted target table
primary_access.scope: The authenticated author laboratory urinary-exosome database contains CHMP2B NP_054762 with four peptides. This is target detection in an isolated preparation, not luminal topology, classical secretion or an exosome-specific MF.

primary_access.access: selected partial despite full flag; genuine external full
primary_access.scope: Independent peer recovered and read original full yeast reconstitution Methods/Results. Vps2 supports recycling/subsequent rounds rather than the initial minimal scission reaction. Independent human CHMP2B deformation supports existing broad fission participation, not a relabeled purified human scission assay.

primary_access.access: abstract-limited review
primary_access.scope: The review provides ESCRT pathway context. Load-bearing target decisions instead cite inspected primary assembly, viral budding, VPS4 binding and mutant-clearance experiments. No full review body or target-specific direct assay is claimed.

primary_access.access: selected partial; indexed full primary Results
primary_access.scope: The actual indexed human ESCRT siRNA Results and Figures1–3 were inspected, including CHMP2B alignment, nuclear morphology, cytokinesis, spindle and centrosome phenotypes. Mechanistic alternatives remain unresolved; extensive VPS4-focused live assays are not relabeled CHMP2B experiments.

primary_access.access: selected partial; literal target assay records
primary_access.scope: Exact BHF-UCL target records resolve CHMP2B association with human TERF2IP/RAP1 by fluorescence complementation in HTC75 cells and GST/FLAG pull-down in HEK293T cells. Complete original Methods were not recovered. Tagged association is supported without transferring telomeric DNA binding, transcriptional or telomere functions to CHMP2B.

primary_access.access: abstract-limited review
primary_access.scope: The review discusses endosome/lysosome/autophagy connections. Exact CHMP2B fusion work remains unresolved and is not established by generic ESCRT membership; independent full mutant-delivery studies retain the pathway connection.

primary_access.access: selected full
primary_access.scope: Actual human HEK293T Flag-CHMP2B/endogenous hSnf7-2 co-IP in Figure6A supports CHMP4B association. Distinguish that experiment from the Snf7 depletion and neuron-cargo analyses.

primary_access.access: selected full/BioC plus literal target records
primary_access.scope: Actual Results/Methods define Y2H screening and LUMIER retesting. Four exact MINT records resolve human CHMP2B with nsp1 and nsp9 processed SARS products: one Y2H and one positive LUMIER record per pair. Target-specific Z-scores1.3/1.1 exceed the stated >1 threshold. The original TableS1 DOC itself was not read; literal curated target records and full primary methods are distinguished.

primary_access.access: selected exact-main abstract; genuine fresh normal full retained separately
primary_access.scope: Fresh normal full Results37/40 and Methods51/55/58 were read. Human C-terminal-His CHMP2B binds defined CHMP4B/CHMP3 constructs by SPR, and depletion combinations support HIV release. The cryo-EM polymer is CHMP2A–CHMP3, not CHMP2B. The protected selected cache remains abstract-only.

primary_access.access: selected full/BioC; target supplement unresolved
primary_access.scope: Full main isolation/MS Methods were read. The exact CHMP2B row in the original prostatic-exosome target supplement remains unrecovered; failed/challenge files are not counted as tables. Independent urinary-exosome detection is kept separate.

primary_access.access: selected abstract; genuine indexed primary Results fragments
primary_access.scope: The inspected original Results concern mutant CHMP2BIntron5 genetic interactions in flies and syntaxin-dependent maturation context. No direct WT CHMP2B–syntaxin interaction or intrinsic fusase activity is established.

primary_access.access: selected full
primary_access.scope: Actual human293T depletion, rescue and EM Results/Methods were read. CHMP2A is the stronger individual EIAV contributor; co-depleting CHMP2B increases the defect. Many rescue/interface experiments test CHMP2A, not CHMP2B.

primary_access.access: abstract/summary only
primary_access.scope: The original plasma-membrane-repair source remains intact; full CHMP2B-specific assays were not recovered here. Independent full2026 human target imaging and toxin-recovery evidence supports retained repair biology, without substituting it as the original experiment.

primary_access.access: selected full
primary_access.scope: Actual Figures1/2 and Methods show endogenous human CHMP2B in cytoplasmic and membrane-associated ESCRT spirals trapped by VPS4 depletion; anti-CHMP2B ab33174. The ultrastructure is deep-etch EM, not cryo-EM. Gag/CHMP2A-specific manipulations are kept distinct.

primary_access.access: selected full plus genuine external BioC
primary_access.scope: Full E-cadherin–BirA proximity-screen Methods/Results were read. The original exact target rows and independent cadherin-binding validation are unresolved. Cytoplasmic target localization is independently supported; proximity is not automatically pair binding.

primary_access.access: selected abstract; partial authentic primary external
primary_access.scope: Publisher Extended Data1/5 legends and pixels were inspected by the independent peer. Exact accessible kinetochore/microtubule panels identify CHMP4B, while another label identifies CHMP2A. Complete main Methods/Results remained inaccessible, so no CHMP2B misattribution or absence is asserted.

primary_access.access: selected main full; genuine full author PDF supplies Methods
primary_access.scope: Actual human HeLa endogenous CHMP2B Figures 1A/1B and Extended Data Figure 1A, Figure 4 and Extended Data 1/9 were read/visually checked. CHMP2B localizes to reforming NE and midbody; cooperative A/B depletion supports reassembly. NPC incorporation is not resolved, and non-NPC sealing channels must not be called nuclear-pore precursors. No isoform assignment is invented. Figure 1C and the non-NPC-channel ultrastructure are separate CHMP2A experiments, not CHMP2B panels.

primary_access.access: selected abstract plus exact association record
primary_access.scope: Literal source-specific CHMP2B–CHMP4B tagged co-IP record supports positive complex association. Full target-specific primary body was not recovered; no purified binary interface or activity transfer is asserted.

primary_access.access: selected full
primary_access.scope: Results24 and surrounding Methods/interaction classification use recombinant human ESCRT-III C-terminal peptides and MIT domains. This supplies genuine ESCRT-family/interaction context for the new current NAS membership assertion, corroborated by independent endogenous target assembly evidence.

primary_access.access: genuine full normal and external primary
primary_access.scope: Human full-length WT and C-terminally tagged CHMP2B produce membrane tubes; N-terminal tagging and L4D/F5D controls affect remodeling. Figures2/6 and selected Methods/Results support bending. Tube morphology does not measure autonomous membrane breakage.

primary_access.access: genuine full normal and external primary
primary_access.scope: Purified human CHMP2B1–154 ΔC after CHMP4B assembly deforms defined membranes; order, concentration and membrane geometry matter. Figure3 and relevant Methods support deformation without proving a universal scission mechanism.

primary_access.access: genuine full normal and external primary
primary_access.scope: Defined CHMP2BΔC1–154 stiffens membranes under the tested conditions, providing countercontext to tubulation. Methods numbering full-length1–222 conflicts with current human213-aa Q9UQN3; that reagent is not silently mapped to a product. Lipid/assembly dependence is retained.

primary_access.access: genuine full normal
primary_access.scope: Full selected human CAL51 target imaging, mutant controls, endogenous tags, toxin-pulse/chase Results and Methods were read. CHMP2B assembles after the initial annexin plug; WT contributes to later recovery of membrane integrity. Non-CNS cell and injury paradigms limit extrapolation. The paper does not establish direct initial Ca-dependent sealing by CHMP2B.

primary_access.access: genuine full normal
primary_access.scope: Human patient fibroblast and tagged cell assays show mutant-associated defects in endosome–lysosome fusion/delivery and altered Rab7 recruitment, while intraluminal EGFR sorting and signaling remain intact. This distinguishes specific endosomal failure from universal loss of every ESCRT activity.

definition.text: A thin cytoplasmic bridge formed between daughter cells at the end of cytokinesis. The midbody forms where the contractile ring constricts, and may persist for some time before finally breaking to complete cytokinesis.
A protein complex providing a discrete opening in the nuclear envelope of a eukaryotic cell, where the inner and outer nuclear membranes are joined.
The directed movement of proteins into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.
The lipid bilayer surrounding the lysosome and separating its contents from the cell cytoplasm.

A small lytic vacuole that has cell cycle-independent morphology found in most animal cells and that contains a variety of hydrolases, most of which have their maximal activities in the pH range 5-6. The contained enzymes display latency if properly isolated. About 40 different lysosomal hydrolases are known and lysosomes have a great variety of morphologies and functions.
The contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.

A prelysosomal endocytic organelle differentiated from early endosomes by lower lumenal pH and different protein composition. Late endosomes are more spherical than early endosomes and are mostly juxtanuclear, being concentrated near the microtubule organizing center.
A type of endosome in which regions of the limiting endosomal membrane invaginate to form internal vesicles; membrane proteins that enter the internal vesicles are sequestered from the cytoplasm.
A vacuole to which materials ingested by endocytosis are delivered.
The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.
Any of the spindle microtubules that attach to the kinetochores of chromosomes by their plus ends, and maneuver the chromosomes during mitotic or meiotic chromosome segregation.
The part of the cytoplasm that does not contain organelles but which does contain other particulate matter, such as protein complexes.
Binding to a protein.
Binding to a specific domain of a protein.
The autophagic process that proceeds via the formation of an autophagosome.
The reformation of the nuclear membranes following their breakdown in the context of a normal process.
A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the separation of a single continuous membrane into two membranes.
The lipid bilayer surrounding a late endosome.
A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the nucleus.
The joining of the lipid bilayer membrane around a vesicle with the lipid bilayer membrane around the vacuole.

An activity in which a protein, or group of proteins, acts to restrict the size of a fenestration in a membrane or membrane system (i.e. restrict the diameter of a hole in a membrane). An example of this is the molecular function is performed by ESCRT-III proteins at the nuclear envelope of fission yeast during anaphase B.
The resealing of a cell plasma membrane after cellular wounding due to, for instance, mechanical stress.

The cellular catabolic process in which cells digest cellular materials, such as organelles and other macromolecular constituents, or non-self materials such as intracellular pathogens. Autophagy serves to provide essential nutrients under conditions of cellular stress; or can remodel intracellular structures during cell differentiation.

The directed movement of substances from late endosomes to the vacuole. In yeast, after transport to the prevacuolar compartment, endocytic content is delivered to the late endosome and on to the vacuole. This pathway is analogous to endosome to lysosome transport.

official_terms.name: ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process via the multivesicular body sorting pathway

definition.text: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein or peptide covalently tagged with ubiquitin, via the multivesicular body (MVB) sorting pathway; ubiquitin-tagged proteins are sorted into MVBs, and delivered to a lysosome/vacuole for degradation.

synonyms.name: ubiquitin-dependent protein breakdown via the multivesicular body pathway
ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process via the MVB pathway
ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolism via the MVB pathway
ubiquitin-dependent protein degradation via the multivesicular body pathway

definition.text: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of mitotic spindle assembly.

synonyms.name: regulation of spindle assembly involved in mitosis

definition.text: A vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. Extracellular exosomes, also simply called exosomes, have a diameter of about 40-100 nm.
The cellular homeostatic process that preserves a neuron in a stable, differentiated functional and structural state.
Binding to cadherin, a type I membrane protein involved in cell adhesion.
The operation of the mind by which an organism becomes aware of objects of thought or perception; it includes the mental activities associated with thinking, learning, and memory.

official_terms.name: viral budding via host ESCRT complex

definition.text: Viral budding which uses a host ESCRT protein complex, or complexes, to mediate the budding process.

synonyms.name: viral budding through the ESCRT machinery

definition.text: The lipid bilayer surrounding an autophagosome, a double-membrane-bounded vesicle in which endogenous cellular material is sequestered.

official_terms.name: late endosome to lysosome transport

definition.text: The directed movement of substances from late endosome to lysosome.

official_terms.comment: an example of this is snapin in mouse (Q9Z266) in PMID:20920792 inferred from mutant phenotype

definition.text: The organelle membrane fusion process in which the membrane of a multivesicular body fuses with a lysosome to create a hybrid organelle.

synonyms.name: fusion of multivesicular body to lysosome

definition.text: The process by which the midbody, the cytoplasmic bridge that connects the two prospective daughter cells, is severed at the end of mitotic cytokinesis, resulting in two separate daughter cells.
Any membrane that is part of an amphisome.

The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a multivesicular body, a type of late endosome in which regions of the limiting endosomal membrane invaginate to form internal vesicles; membrane proteins that enter the internal vesicles are sequestered from the cytoplasm.

Removal of PI3P and Atg8/LC3 after the closure of the phagophore and before the fusion with the endosome/lysosome (e.g. mammals and insects) or vacuole (yeast), and that very likely destabilizes other Atg proteins and thus enables their efficient dissociation and recycling.
The disaggregation of an ESCRT III complex into its constituent components.

A complex with membrane scission activity that plays a major role in many processes where membranes are remodelled - including endosomal transport (vesicle budding), nuclear envelope organisation (membrane closure, mitotic bridge cleavage), and cytokinesis (abscission).

synonyms.name: endosomal sorting complex required for transport

official_terms.name: kinetochore

definition.text: A multisubunit complex that is located at the centromeric region of DNA and provides an attachment point for the spindle microtubules.

official_terms.comment: Note that the kinetochore overlaps the centromeric DNA, but centromeric DNA is not part of the kinetochore.

definition.text: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of endosomes.
The directed movement of substances into, out of or within a vacuole.
The dissemination of mature viral particles from a host cell, e.g. by cell lysis or the budding of virus particles from the cell membrane.

A chromosome localization process whereby chromosomes are positioned in a specific order and orientation at the metaphase plate (spindle equator), during mitotic chromosome segregation. This alignment ensures that each daughter cell will receive the correct number of chromosomes during cell division.

Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of centrosome duplication. Centrosome duplication is the replication of a centrosome, a structure comprised of a pair of centrioles and peri-centriolar material from which a microtubule spindle apparatus is organized.
A viral budding that starts with formation of a curvature in the host plasma membrane around which the virion particle assembles.

synonyms.name: plasma membrane viral budding during viral capsid envelopment
viral budding from plasma membrane by viral capsid envelopment
viral budding from plasma membrane during viral capsid envelopment
virus budding from plasma membrane by viral capsid envelopment
virus budding from plasma membrane during viral capsid envelopment

official_terms.name: endosome transport via multivesicular body sorting pathway

definition.text: The directed movement of substances from endosomes to lysosomes or vacuoles by a pathway in which molecules are sorted into multivesicular bodies, which then fuse with the target compartment.

synonyms.name: endosome transport via MVB sorting pathway

definition.text: The lipid bilayer surrounding a multivesicular body.

A vesicle-mediated transport process in which transmembrane proteins are ubiquitylated to facilitate their entry into luminal vesicles of multivesicular bodies (MVBs); upon subsequent fusion of MVBs with lysosomes or vacuoles, the cargo proteins are degraded.

The double lipid bilayer that encloses the nucleus, separating its contents from the cytoplasm. It consists of an inner and outer nuclear membrane, with an intermembrane space (20-40 nm wide, also called the perinuclear space) between them. The envelope is supported by the nuclear lamina and contains nuclear pore complexes, which regulate molecular transport.
Binding to an ATPase, any enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of ATP.

An activity in which a protein, or group of proteins, acts to restrict the size of a fenestration in a membrane or membrane system (i.e. restrict the diameter of a hole in a membrane). An example of this is the molecular function is performed by ESCRT-III proteins at the nuclear envelope of fission yeast during anaphase B.
The activity of bending or deforming a membrane. This activity can occur by multiple mechanisms including the insertion amphipathic domains into one or both leaflets.
Binding to a virion, either by binding to components of the capsid or the viral envelope.

viral_binding_term_scope: GO0046790 is virion binding, not general nsp1/nsp9 protein binding; no virion-binding refinement is proposed.

description.text:
Snf7 family members are small coil-coiled proteins that share protein sequence similarity with budding yeast Snf7, which is part of the ESCRT-III complex that is required for endosome-mediated trafficking via multivesicular body (MVB) formation and sorting [[cite:PUB00071227]].

Proteins in this entry also includes human CHMPs (charged multivesicular body proteins), budding yeast Did4/Did2, Arabidopsis vacuolar protein sorting-associated proteins and the archaean Sulfolobus acidocaldarius cell division protein B which is a component required for cell division, forming polymers with segregating nucleoids [[cite:PUB00083231]].

PUB00071227.title: Protein-protein interactions of ESCRT complexes in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
